prompt_md: Two cards each hide a uniformly random number from 0 to 1. You see the first, then keep it or switch to the unseen second. With best play, chance you get the larger?
prompt_short: See one random number, keep it or switch. Best chance of the larger?
hint_md: Keep big numbers, switch small ones. Where's the cutoff?
explain_intuition_md: Without looking it is a coin flip, so 50% is tempting. But seeing the first number helps: keep it if it is above one half, otherwise switch. A high first number usually beats the hidden card and a low one usually loses to it, which lifts your chance to 3 in 4.
explain_math_md: Keep the first card when $x > t$: $$P(t) = \int_t^1 x \, dx + \int_0^t (1 - x) \, dx = \tfrac12 + t - t^2,$$ which peaks at $t = \tfrac12$ with $P = \tfrac34$.
